newsitem.title: USA: Texas residents sue Crown on pollution charges.
newsitem.headline: Texas residents sue Crown on pollution charges.

text.p: Residents living around Crown Central Petroleum Corp's Pasadena, Texas, refinery filed a class action lawsuit against Crown Wednesday charging it with pollution and damaging their homes and health.

The suit, filed in state court in Harris County, Texas, is seeking unspecified compensatory damages, and at least $50 million in punitive damages, said the lawyers representing the 77 residents in the suit.
Crown spokesman Joe Coale said the company could not immediately comment on the filing because it had not yet seen the legal documents.
The residents are represented by Houston-based Maierson Law Firm, P.C., which specializes in toxic tort litigation.
The firm said the suit was brought to seek damages for alleged adverse health effects, diminution of property value and excessive noise and odor from the refinery.
The suit is separate from a federal lawsuit a coalition of environmental group and citizens have threatened to bring against Crown for emissions at Pasadena and allegedly polluting the environment.
The refinery can process up to 100,000 barrels per day of crude oil.
((-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212-859-1631))
